transcript:
Meeting: POC Weekly Caching Sync - Week 7
Date: 2025-10-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Hannah Li, Tom Becker, Janelle Park (Redwood) - Dana Ross, Samir Patel, Priya Sharma, Evan Liu (Nimbus)

Summary: quick review of last week's pilot numbers, focusing on prefix vs KV cache hit rates, prompt reuse strategy and next steps for canonicalization and replay. Some noisy transcription; names and product terms may be slightly off.

Topics:
- KV cache hit rates (per-model)
- Prefix cache vs full-request caching tradeoffs
- Prompt normalization / canonicalization strategy
- Eviction policy and sizing recommendations
- Next steps / replay & benchmark plan

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok good morning, good afternoon, everybody thanks for joining. quick agenda - results from the last 7 days of the pilot, hit rates, ideas for improving prefix reuse, and then next steps. Dana you good to start?
[00:18] Dana Ross: yeah all good thanks Maya. um we'll just jump in, Samir has the numbers and Evan has infra notes.
[00:24] Samir Patel: hey folks, so we looked at two things primarily: prefix cache and the per-request KV cache where we stash full prompt keys. baseline week (pre-change) our effective cache hit rate across models was around 18-22%, after Redwood's canonicalization patch and relaxed TTLs we saw an increase to about 47% overall. that's a big jump but still a ways to go.
[00:43] Luis Ortega: quick clarif — when you say "canonicalization patch" do you mean the prompt normalization that normalizes whitespace and user metadata?
[00:50] Samir Patel: yeah, exactly. we stripped session tokens from the keys, normalized timestamps and user-id fragments, removed device metadata. so the key space compressed a lot.
[00:58] [01:02] Maya Chen: nice. can you break that 47% down into prefix vs KV?
[01:06] Samir Patel: sure. prefix cache (we're using Redwood prefix cache) accounted for about 28% hit rate; KV (full prompt) hits were another 19% — but interestingly the larger model we have, retail-chat-xl, had higher prefix reuse but lower KV because prompts vary more.
[01:24] Tom Becker: on the infra side, our KV nodes saw bursts. we had a few hundredthousands requests per hour at peak, read latency was OK but writes spiked. we suspect some churn due to slightly different keys.
[01:35] Janelle Park: one idea is canonical templates for the front-end - push more of the variable stuff into structured fields that don't get concatenated into the prompt. that reduces unique keys a lot.
[01:44] Priya Sharma: yeah we can do that; product is on board to change the template. question on TTL — what's the recommendation? we were using 5 minutes before, increased to 20 in the pilot.
[01:54] Luis Ortega: TTL is workload dependent; for shopping flows where users often iterate within minutes, 20-30 minutes seems reasonable. for personalization flows where freshness matters I'd keep it shorter. also consider per-key TTLs — e.g., session prompts longer, user-profile-based keys shorter.
[02:12] Evan Liu: what's the eviction policy? we're on default LRU with 32GB per node. during peaks eviction churn seems high.
[02:20] Tom Becker: correct, LRU 32GB. we could increase memory but cost goes up. also multi-tenant collisions are concerning.
[02:27] Maya Chen: cost tradeoff — Redwood Optimize can estimate dollars saved per percentage point of hit rate increase given your token mix. Janelle, can you capture?
[02:34] Janelle Park: yep we'll send a delta-cost estimate.
[02:36] [03:00] Samir Patel: additional metric we noticed: warm-start hit rate. when users repeat prompts in the same session, prefix hits are much higher, 60-70% in some cohorts. so driving prompt reuse inside sessions is high-leverage.
[03:15] Maya Chen: good - that suggests UI changes + frontend normalization will be quick wins. can you do a small A/B testing?
[03:20] Priya Sharma: yes we can. we'll roll to 10% of traffic first.
[03:24] Luis Ortega: other tuning: key hashing with canonicalized tokens reduces key length and speeds KV lookups a bit. also grouping similar prefixes into a single canonical prefix key (i.e., bucketization) is useful particularly for product detail vs search flows.
[03:38] Dana Ross: what about model routing? some of our requests hit a larger model by default, and that model has lower reuse. can Redwood route lighter-weight requests to a smaller variant to boost hit rates and reduce cost?
[03:48] Maya Chen: yes that's something we can configure: route by intent or latency budget. small models get higher cache reuse typically, and response time is lower. we can propose a routing policy for the pilot.
[03:58] Samir Patel: slight transcrip noise here, but also saw that when we used function calling and structured responses, token variance dropped and hit rates improved.
[04:08] Luis Ortega: note on KV sizing: for your QPS profile, recommending moving to 64GB nodes (or add an extra node), set max-ttl at 6 hours for session bundles, and lower retention for ephemeral prompts. also enable async writes if you can tolerate eventual consistency to smooth spikes.
[04:26] Evan Liu: async writes could be tricky for correctness — we'll evaluate.
[04:28] [04:45] Maya Chen: let's recap concrete next steps and owners. Luis, export the per-model KV hit logs and send to Samir and Maya. Samir, run the 48-hour replay with canonicalization and the new TTLs on a staging KV cluster and share results. Janelle, send cost delta. Maya will send the recommended routing policy doc and sample canonicalization script.
[05:05] Priya Sharma: timeline realistic?
[05:08] Maya Chen: yes - aiming for 48h replay by next week, cost delta and configs by Friday.
[05:12] [05:13] Action items (in-call):
- Luis: export detailed per-model KV hit logs and send CSV by 2025-10-09
- Samir: run 48h replay with canonicalization patch and share results by 2025-10-14
- Maya: send updated pricing impact estimate for increased cache capacity by 2025-10-10
- Janelle: provide routing policy draft and cost delta by 2025-10-10

Questions:
Q: how do we measure correctness impact of canonicalization?
A: we need side-by-side eval set; Redwood suggests sampling the outputs pre/post and flagging for stability - can run automated evals on a subset.

References / Links shared:
- Pilot results dashboard (internal link): https://redwood.company/s/dashboards/nimbus-cache-week7    
- Sample canonicalization script (shared in chat)
- KV sizing doc: https://redwood.company/docs/kv-sizing

Close: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next Wednesday same time for a quick health check unless something urgent pops up.

Note: transcript has some imperfect speaker labels and occasional mis-typed product names; please rely on the metadata for owners and next steps.
